verdict.rationale: Temporal's own Client API lets a program start Workflow Executions, send Signals and Queries, and retrieve results, which covers 'activate'. Worker Versioning lets updated workflow code be rolled out programmatically. However, Temporal is explicitly Workflows-as-Code, so workflow definitions are written and deployed as code on Workers rather than created or updated as resources through a public API, and no OpenAPI spec was found. missing for 10: API-level creation of workflow definitions, API-level updating of definitions independent of code deployment, a documented public REST/OpenAPI surface, hands-on evidence of an agent driving this end to end.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can have an agent create, update, and activate a workflow programmatically through the public API

citations.quote: enabling you to start Workflow Executions, send Signals and Queries, and retrieve results
The Worker Versioning feature allows you to tag your Workers and programmatically roll them out in versioned deployments
A Schedule contains instructions for starting a Workflow Execution at specific times.
